conventions: בְּנֵי נֵכָר -> *aliens* (144.7, 144.11) is one fused unit under rule 30, headed on נֵכָר under rule 23, since the single English word writes that noun's lexeme alone; the chain's *of* is the rectum's under rule 19 and בֵּן is not marked unrepresented beside it.

Where a Hebrew substantive is rendered by a two-word English phrase closing on a class noun, this chapter read the class noun as rule 31's supplied generic and headed on the modifier: יָמִין -> *right hand* on *right* (144.8 twice, 144.11 twice), מִשְׂגָּב -> *My high tower* on *high* (144.2), זָוִית -> *corner stones* on *corner* (144.12). The competing head is named in each unit's note under rule 8. Corpus precedent agrees: יָמִין -> *right hand* heads on *right* in 42 units against two on *hand*.

144.3 writes two waws and three ASV connectives (*that*, *Or*, *that*). Both waws take the *that* standing where they stand, and the disjunctive *Or*, which opens a colon the Hebrew juxtaposes with no conjunction in it, is the surplus and is `added` under rule 14's closing sentences. The competing allocation gives *Or* to the second waw and marks the second *that* added; the first colon's identical waw -> *that* decides it.

The datives לִי (144.2, beside מָגִנִּי, which carries the one written *My* on its own suffix) and לּוֹ (144.15, the ASV writing *in such a case* for כָּכָה alone) are each unrepresented together with their suffixes, the ASV's recasting writing nothing for either morpheme. These four tokens are four of the five BSB disagreements.
report: Checked all 16 candidate lemma groups; none is a split. Every multi-treatment bucket is licensed by the ASV's own wording or by a difference in the source: the article buckets divide only where the ASV writes a *the* in one colon and none in the next (בֶּהָרִים -> *the mountains* against לַמְּלָכִים -> *unto kings*, הָעָם -> *the people* against לַקְרָב -> *to war*); the participial הַ takes *Who* in 144.2 and 144.10 and *he that* in 144.10 according to what the ASV wrote in the article's place, which is what rule 41 asks; לְ divides *to*/*unto*/*of* and מִן divides *from*/*out of* on the English word alone; *thy*/*thine* is orthography.

Read the dump end to end for what the lemma table is blind to, the 11 `added` units, and set each against the places the chapter folded a supplied word into a licensing morpheme. Supplied connectives are `added` in exactly the cola that write no conjunction (1 *And*, 3 *Or*, 12 *And*, 13 *When*/*And*/*and*, 14 *When* twice, 15 *Yea*), while all seven waws standing in the chapter take the connective written for them (3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 11, 14) and the אֲשֶׁר of 12 takes its *When*. Supplied determiners, generic nouns, vocative *O*s and English phrasal particles are folded into their licensing morphemes without exception, so nothing is folded in one verse and marked added in another.

Copula placement is uniform: on the predicate morpheme wherever one stands (בָּרוּךְ 1, מָה 3, יְמִין 8 and 11, מָלֵא 13, סָבַל 14, אֶשֶׁר and אֱלֹהָיו 15), on the preposition heading a prepositional predicate under rule 49 (כְּ 4 and 12), and on the predicate participle rather than the article under rule 41 in 10, where the supplied *Thou* is `added` because no morpheme in that verse denotes the addressee and rule 10 makes the verse the whole unit of work.

The two repeated passages are aligned identically, unit for unit and head for head: 144.8 against the second half of 144.11 (relative plus resumptive suffix fused as one *Whose*, the rewritten *whose* to the suffix on יְמִינָם under rule 22's coordinated-clause paragraph, both יָמִין phrases headed on *right*), and מִיַּד בְּנֵי נֵכָר in 144.7 against 144.11 (*out of* on מִן headed on *out*, supplied *the* on the construct, the pair fused to *aliens*).

BSB: all five disagreements are documented convention differences, not errors. בֶּ in 144.5 is rule 40's promoted object, which that rule names in its own words (*Touch the mountains*); לִי with its suffix in 144.2 and לּוֹ with its suffix in 144.15 are datives the ASV's recasting leaves with no English at all, the one written *My* in 144.2 answering to מָגִנִּי's own suffix. None should be moved to lift the rate.

No promotion. בְּנֵי נֵכָר -> *aliens* is already provided for, rule 23 naming a construct chain among the things rule 30 fuses and settling the head where one lexeme alone is written; the supplied *Thou* of 144.10 is decided by rule 25's closing sentences read with rule 10; the שֶׁ plus suffix -> *whose* of 144.15 falls under rule 22, which is written on the condition and not on the lemma אֲשֶׁר.
